row.evidence: Keeper's pricing page lists "Advanced provisioning (SCIM, AD/LDAP, SSO/SAML)" only under Enterprise ($6.00/user/month billed annually); Business Starter ($2.00) and Business ($4.00) do not include SCIM.
row.notes: Pricing page now lists Enterprise at $6.00/user/month billed annually (June: ~$6, Contact Sales); a 'Request a Quote' button remains. Team plan changed from Business ($4) to Business Starter ($2, 'Protection for 5–10 users') under the v3 rule that team_plan is the cheapest paid multi-user tier, so the multiplier is 3.0 (6/2); against Business it would be 1.5. SSO (SAML 2.0), SCIM, AD/LDAP Bridge, CLI and the Developer SDKs/REST API are all Enterprise-only in the comparison table (tier mapping read from the table's check-mark cells; icons are not quotable). SCIM 2.0 endpoint per Keeper node with a Keeper-generated bearer token; SCIM DELETE and active=false lock the user rather than deleting. SCIM requires a reserved email domain. SCIM can be used without SSO (JumpCloud guide). New users arrive as 'invited' and teams as 'pending' until approved by an admin login, Commander or Keeper Automator (zero-knowledge key sharing).

auth.token_source: Admin Console > node > Provisioning > Add Method > SCIM > Generate (token shown once)

operations.notes: SCIM DELETE /Users/{id} locks the user instead of deleting; permanent deletion only in the Admin Console or Commander. Groups map to Keeper Teams; Groups DELETE deletes the team.

deprovision.data_retained: Account is locked; the user's owned records are retained and shared records stay accessible to other users and teams

pagination.notes: Default response capped at 1000 entries; startIndex/count pagination on Users and Groups GET.

attributes.notes: Attribute list taken from Keeper's documented POST/PUT example bodies, which declare the enterprise extension schema but set no enterprise attributes; 'roles' is accepted but not used by Keeper. Username must be a valid email.

roles.how: SCIM roles attribute is ignored; roles are assigned via Team-to-Role mapping on SCIM-provisioned teams (not for administrative roles)

limitations.text: SCIM provisioning only accepted for email domains reserved to the Keeper tenant.
Users are created in an 'invited' state and teams/team memberships in a 'pending' state until approved by an admin login, Keeper Commander team-approve or the Keeper Automator service.
One node per identity provider; SCIM on a node does not control its sub-nodes.
Entra connector: emails and userName must share the same source value; user deletes not supported, only disable (lock).
Provisioning beyond purchased seats is rejected with HTTP 428.

auth.notes: Commander logs in as a Keeper admin account; Service Mode exposes the session behind an api-key header with configurable expiry and per-key command allow-lists.

capabilities.notes: Capabilities are Commander CLI/SDK commands (enterprise-user, create-user, enterprise-team, enterprise-role), not REST resources; Service Mode runs these commands over HTTP.

endpoints.purpose: Commander Service Mode: queue any allowed Commander command (e.g. enterprise-user --add/--lock/--delete)
Commander Service Mode v1: run an allowed Commander command synchronously

audit_log_api.notes: Event export to SIEMs requires the Advanced Reporting & Alerts Module add-on.

limitations.text: No hosted vendor REST user API: the documented REST interface is a self-hosted wrapper around the Commander CLI session.

google.notes: Google Admin 'Keeper Web (SAML)' app; Google's SCIM provisions users only, groups need Keeper's Google Cloud Function.

onelogin.notes: Per Keeper's guide; OneLogin's own connector page not loaded.

fallbacks.other_sync: Keeper Bridge AD/LDAP sync (Enterprise); Google Workspace Cloud Function sync; email auto-provisioning
